name: SDR Fundamentals & Operation
description: Ability to operate software-defined radio platforms for signal reception, transmission, and analysis. Covers SDR hardware configuration, gain and bandwidth tuning, antenna selection, frequency calibration, and integration with signal processing toolchains such as GNU Radio and SDR#. Foundational skill for all wireless security work in the lab.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to software-defined radio hardware or concepts

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands SDR concepts, frequency spectrum basics, and the role of SDR in wireless security
evidence: Completed SDR fundamentals training or equivalent coursework
Can explain the difference between direct-sampling and superheterodyne SDR architectures
Understands Nyquist sampling, bandwidth, and center frequency concepts

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Operates SDR hardware under supervision to receive and visualize known signals
evidence: Configured and operated USRP or HackRF under guidance for signal reception
Built basic GNU Radio flowgraphs for signal visualization
Tuned SDR parameters (gain, sample rate, bandwidth) to receive target signals under supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently configures and operates SDR platforms for a range of reception and analysis tasks
evidence: Independently configured SDR hardware for 3+ different signal types across distinct frequency bands
Selected appropriate antennas and front-end filtering for target frequency ranges
Calibrated SDR frequency accuracy and documented measurement uncertainty
Produced repeatable signal captures with documented parameters

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex SDR configurations; integrates multiple SDR platforms; mentors junior analysts
evidence: Configured multi-channel or MIMO SDR setups for simultaneous monitoring
Developed custom GNU Radio blocks or SDR automation scripts for lab use
Troubleshot and resolved SDR hardware and software integration issues
Reviews SDR capture setups and mentors junior staff on hardware operation

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines lab SDR methodology and hardware standards; designs custom SDR solutions
evidence: Evaluated and selected lab SDR hardware platforms and established configuration standards
Designed custom SDR receive chains for specialized lab requirements
Published research or developed novel SDR-based security analysis techniques
Trains teams on SDR operation and maintains lab SDR methodology documentation

assessment_methods.description: Observe configuration and operation of SDR hardware for a specified signal reception task
Receive, identify, and document three different signal types across VHF/UHF/microwave bands using lab SDR equipment
